name: strcat
description: Appends the string from to the end of the string to. Returns a pointer to the resulting null-terminated string. The to buffer must be large enough.

args.name: to
args.desc: Destination string; from is appended to its end

args.name: from
args.desc: String appended to the end of to

name: strchr
description: Finds the first occurrence of character c in string. Returns a pointer to that character, or NULL if not found. In VuGen, the result should be cast to (char *).

name: strcmp
description: Compares two strings case-sensitively to determine their alphabetical order. Returns <0 if string1 is less than string2, 0 if they are equal, and >0 if string1 is greater.

name: strcpy
description: Copies the string source to dest, including the null terminator. Returns the destination string. Make sure the dest buffer is large enough.

name: strdup
description: Duplicates a string into newly allocated memory and returns it. Useful for making a modifiable copy of a static buffer (for example the result of lr_whoami); the copy must be released with free().

name: stricmp
description: Compares two strings case-insensitively. Returns <0, 0, or >0 according to the alphabetical order of string1 relative to string2.

name: strlen
description: Returns the length of the string in bytes, excluding the null terminator.

name: strncat
description: Appends at most n characters from from_string to the end of to_string. Returns a pointer to the resulting null-terminated string.

args.name: from_string
args.desc: Source string of the characters to append

name: strncmp
signature: int strncmp(const char *string1, const char *string2, size_t n);
description: Compares the first n characters of two strings (case-sensitive). Returns <0, 0, or >0 according to alphabetical order.

name: strncpy
description: Copies the first n characters of source to dest and returns a pointer to dest. Note: a null terminator is not added automatically if source is longer than n.

name: strnicmp
signature: int strnicmp(const char *string1, const char *string2, size_t num);
description: Compares the first num characters of two strings case-insensitively. Returns <0, 0, or >0 according to alphabetical order.

name: strrchr
description: Finds the last occurrence of character c in string. Returns a pointer to that character, or NULL if not found. In VuGen, the result should be cast to (char *).

name: strspn
description: Returns the length of the initial segment of string that consists entirely of characters in skipset. Counting stops at the first character not in skipset.

name: strstr
description: Finds the first occurrence of string2 within string1. Returns a pointer to that position, or NULL if not found. In VuGen, the result should be cast to (char *).

args.name: string2
args.desc: String to search for within string1

name: strtok
description: Returns the next token from string, separated by any of the characters in delimiters. After the first call, pass NULL as string to get subsequent tokens; returns NULL when no tokens remain. VuGen note: declare "extern char* strtok(char *token, const char *delimiter);" at the top of the script and cast the result to (char *).

args.name: string
args.desc: String to split into tokens (NULL to continue)

name: memchr
signature: void *memchr(const void *s, int c, size_t n);
description: Searches the first n bytes of buffer s for character c. Returns a pointer to the first occurrence, or NULL if not found.

args.name: n
args.desc: Number of leading bytes of the buffer to examine

name: memcmp
signature: int memcmp(const void *s1, const void *s2, size_t n);
description: Compares the first n bytes of two buffers. Returns <0 if s1 is less than s2, 0 if they are identical, and >0 if s1 is greater.

name: memcpy
signature: void *memcpy( void *dest, const void *src, size_t n );
description: Copies n bytes from buffer src to buffer dest and returns the dest pointer. The src and dest areas must not overlap (use memmove in that case).

name: memmove
signature: void *memmove( void *dest, const void *src, size_t n );
description: Moves n bytes from buffer src to dest and returns the dest pointer. Safe to use when the source and destination areas overlap.

name: memset
signature: void *memset( void *buffer, int c, size_t n);
description: Fills the first n bytes of buffer with character c and returns the buffer pointer. Commonly used to zero out a buffer or struct.

name: calloc
description: Allocates an array and initializes all its elements to zero. Returns a pointer to the memory, or NULL if allocation fails or either argument is 0. Release with free().

args.name: elem_size
args.desc: Size of each element in bytes

name: free
description: Frees a block of heap memory allocated by calloc or malloc. Returns no value.

name: malloc
description: Allocates a block of memory of num_bytes bytes. Returns NULL on failure or if num_bytes is 0; the block must be released with free(). VuGen note: very large local variables (e.g. char buffer[4096*8]) trigger a "Too many local variables" error, so use malloc() for large buffers.

args.name: num_bytes
args.desc: Size of the memory block in bytes

name: realloc
description: Resizes a previously allocated memory block. Returns a pointer to the allocated space, or NULL if it fails or any argument is 0.

name: atof
description: Converts a string to a floating-point value by reading the leading portion of the string up to the first non-numeric character. Returns 0.0 on error; the result is undefined on overflow.

name: atoi
description: Converts a string to an integer by reading the leading portion of the string up to the first non-numeric character. Returns 0 on error; the result is undefined on overflow.

name: atol
description: Converts a string to a long integer by reading the leading portion of the string up to the first non-numeric character. Returns 0 on error; the result is undefined on overflow.

name: strtol
signature: long strtol(const char *string, char **endptr, int radix);
description: Converts a string to a long integer using the given radix; leading whitespace is ignored and scanning stops at the first non-numeric character. Returns LONG_MAX/LONG_MIN on overflow and 0 if no conversion could be performed.

args.name: endptr
args.desc: Address of a pointer set to the position where scanning stopped

args.name: radix
args.desc: Number base (0 or 2-36); 0 = determined from the prefix (0x hex, 0 octal, 1-9 decimal)

name: sprintf
description: Writes formatted output to a string. Returns the number of characters written, or a negative value on failure. The destination buffer must be large enough; a buffer overflow can cause the script to behave unpredictably.

args.name: string_buffer
args.desc: Destination buffer for the formatted result

name: sscanf
signature: int sscanf(const char *buffer, const char *format_string, args);
description: Reads formatted input from a string. Returns the number of items successfully read (not counting ignored fields).

args.name: format_string
args.desc: Format string that controls how the input is parsed

args.name: args
args.desc: Addresses of the variables that receive the parsed values

name: tolower
description: Converts a character to lowercase and returns the result. Non-alphabetic characters are unchanged.

name: toupper
description: Converts a character to uppercase and returns the result. Non-alphabetic characters are unchanged.

name: isdigit
description: Checks whether a character is a decimal digit ('0' to '9'). Returns a nonzero value (true) if it is, zero (false) otherwise.

name: isalpha
description: Checks whether a character is a letter (A-Z or a-z). Returns a nonzero value (true) if it is, zero (false) otherwise.
